mainEntity.name: Should adults use fluoride toothpaste every day?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, current UK dental guidelines recommend that adults brush twice daily with a toothpaste containing at least 1,350 ppm fluoride. Daily use helps maintain a consistent level of fluoride at the tooth surface, supporting the natural remineralisation process and reducing the risk of decay. For best results, spit out excess toothpaste after brushing rather than rinsing with water, as this allows the fluoride to remain in contact with your teeth for longer. If you have questions about which toothpaste is most suitable, your dentist can advise based on your individual oral health.

mainEntity.name: Is fluoride safe for adults to use long term?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fluoride used at recommended levels in dental products is considered safe for long-term use by major health organisations worldwide, including the British Dental Association and the World Health Organisation. The concentrations in toothpaste and professional treatments are carefully regulated. Safety concerns typically relate to ingestion of excessive quantities, which is not a risk associated with normal use of dental products. If you have particular health conditions or concerns, discussing them with your dentist ensures that any recommendations are tailored to your individual circumstances and medical history.

mainEntity.name: Can fluoride reverse tooth decay in adults?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fluoride can help reverse very early stages of tooth decay — specifically when demineralisation has begun but a cavity has not yet formed. By promoting the redeposition of calcium and phosphate into weakened enamel, fluoride can help repair these early lesions. However, once a cavity has physically developed in the tooth structure, fluoride alone cannot restore it, and restorative dental treatment is typically required. This is why regular dental examinations are valuable — they allow early signs of enamel weakening to be identified and managed before they progress to the point of requiring more extensive treatment.

mainEntity.name: Do I need professional fluoride treatment if I already use fluoride toothpaste?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not all adults require professional fluoride treatment. For many patients, daily use of fluoride toothpaste provides sufficient protection. However, professional fluoride application may be recommended for adults who have a higher risk of decay — for example, those with dry mouth, extensive dental restorations, exposed root surfaces, or a history of frequent cavities. Your dentist will assess your individual risk factors during a clinical examination and advise whether additional fluoride treatment would be beneficial. The decision is always based on your specific oral health needs rather than a one-size-fits-all approach.

mainEntity.name: Are there alternatives to fluoride for preventing tooth decay?

acceptedAnswer.text: While some products marketed as fluoride-free alternatives exist, the evidence supporting fluoride for decay prevention is significantly stronger than for any currently available substitute. Ingredients such as hydroxyapatite are being researched and show some promise, but fluoride remains the gold standard in preventative dentistry based on decades of robust clinical evidence. Good oral hygiene, dietary management, and regular dental visits all contribute to decay prevention alongside fluoride. If you prefer to explore alternative products, discussing your options with a dental professional ensures you receive balanced, evidence-based guidance.

mainEntity.name: Why are my teeth still getting cavities if I use fluoride toothpaste?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fluoride toothpaste significantly reduces the risk of decay, but it does not eliminate it entirely. Cavities develop due to a combination of factors including diet, oral bacteria, brushing technique, saliva quality, and individual susceptibility. If you are experiencing recurrent decay despite using fluoride toothpaste, it may be worth reviewing your brushing and flossing technique, dietary habits, and overall oral hygiene routine with your dentist or hygienist. They can identify specific contributing factors and recommend targeted strategies — which may include professional fluoride treatment — to help better protect your teeth going forward.
